To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

weathering rates are high in the south of Sweden and low in the north, that the weathering rates are generally high enough to sustain whole-tree harvesting in the southern parts of Sweden, but not in the central and northern regions, and that there is a need to improve the knowledge about the weathering rates and their spatial and temporal variation in order to make sustainable forest management possible in Sweden.

the weathering rates in the majority of sites are sufficient to sustain the present level of harvest, but that there are a few sites where the weathering rates are too low, and that these should be avoided for whole-tree harvesting.
